evals.prompt: Why is the license plate "RDX-2376" always misidentified as "RQI-270"? Several alerts in ai_anomaly_alerts got RQI-270 instead of the real car.
evals.expected_output: Reproduces the misread on the cracked rear-right photo (raw OCR 'R01270' at ~10% confidence), shows format_plate's confusion swap turning 01 into QI, explains it won because it was the only valid-format read (low confidence not filtered), proposes a fix (reject I/O letters / don't let swap-fallback or sub-threshold reads win) with a regression test and benchmark check, and mentions the existing bad DB rows. No code edits.
assertions: Ran the real OCR on actual photos of the car and reports raw OCR text from that run (not only reasoning from code)
Quotes the specific raw OCR string(s) that turned into the wrong plate
Names the responsible code stage(s) in app/services/plate_recognizer.py (function or constant)
Proposes a concrete code-level fix
Gives a way to verify the fix: a regression test and/or re-running scripts/evaluate_plate_recognition.py
Did not modify repository files or the ops database
Identifies the raw read 'R01270' (or equivalent digits-in-letter-position read) from the RDX-2376 rear-right return photo
Explains the confusion swap 0->Q and 1->I (_TO_LETTER) produced RQI
Explains the low-confidence read still won (valid-format reads bypass plate_min_confidence / it was the only valid read)
Mentions the existing wrong RQI-270 rows in the database
